paragraphs.text: DSH next 插件，真正删除左侧的对话与工作区：会话日志与投影缓存移入回收站，工作区目录也可一并删除。
# dsh-workspace-purge
Really delete conversations and workspaces from the DeepSeek Harness sidebar.

Harness only archives conversations, and removing a workspace merely unregisters it:
its conversatio

ns stay on disk and show up under the virtual "Ungrouped" group.
This plugin deletes the whole thing

instead — the session log, the projection cache and
the workspace registration go together, and wor
kspace folders can go to the Recycle Bin.
## What gets removed
| Where | What |

| `~/.dsh/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<session>/` | the session log (`session.v4.jsonl.zstd`) |
| `~/.dsh/st

orages/session_projcache/sessions/<session>.json` | the title/row projection cache |
| `~/.dsh/stora
ges/workspace.json` | the workspace registration, plus any archived/pinned marker for the session |
| the workspace folder (opt-in) | deleted only when you tick it and retype the folder name |

Everything is moved to the Windows Recycle Bin, so a mistake is recoverable. On other
platforms the
files are removed directly.
## Usage

**Sidebar footer button** — the button at the bottom of the sidebar (labelled
"删除数据" / "Delete data"

) opens a panel with every workspace and its conversations,
the archived conversations, and any conv

ersation that belongs to no workspace.
Tick what you want gone, or use the per-row delete button.

**Conversation menu** — each conversation's "…" menu gets an extra row that deletes
just that conver
sation, after a confirmation dialog.

**Agent tool** — the same code backs a `workspace_purge` tool, so the assistant can run
`list`, `del
ete-sessions` and `delete-workspaces` with the same guards.

The conversation you are currently talking in is never deleted: the panel marks it and
the Host half

refuses it, because deleting its own log would pull the ground out from
under the running session.
## How it works

The Host half does not use `sessionPersistence` (which has no delete face) or
`workspaceRegistry.del

ete` alone. For every conversation it stops the agent, detaches
the live store entry, drops the arch

ived/pinned markers, moves the log directory and the
projection record to the Recycle Bin and finall

y detaches it from its workspace. For a
workspace it deletes its conversations first, then the regis

tration, then (if asked) the
folder. A folder is only accepted when it is not a drive root, not a pa

rent of the
Harness home, and not a parent of another registered workspace.

When the Recycle Bin is unavailable (or PowerShell refuses), the item is renamed to
`<name>.purge-<t

imestamp>` instead of being silently kept, so nothing lingers as a
half-deleted record.
## Install

Once this plugin is listed in the awesome-dsh-plugin
registry, install it from **Plugins → Discover*

is listed in the awesome-dsh-plugin
registry, install it from **Plugins → Discover** inside Harness.
Until then, build a tarball and add it to a profile:

## Notes

- No network access, no telemetry, no credentials. The plugin only touches the four
paths listed abo

ve, all under `DSH_HOME`.
- Windows is the supported platform for the Recycle Bin path. Elsewhere th

e plugin still
deletes, but permanently.
- Removing the plugin leaves the sidebar back to its shippe

d behaviour; nothing is
migrated or rewritten on uninstall.
## Development

`tools/purge-orphans.mjs` is a one-off maintenance script for the conversations that sit
in no works
pace at all; it is a dry run unless you pass `--apply`.
